number_of_offences: Charged under Sections 20, 25 and 29 of the NDPS Act; upheld as completed offences
key_evidence_accepted: The recovery of ganja was made from the four co-accused, including 'NE'. The prosecution relied on the statement of 'NE', the confessional statement of the appellant, and the bank statements of 'VS' @ 'B' who allegedly disclosed money transferred to the appellant.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as having provided statements that were part of the prosecution's case, but noted that the prosecution has not recovered anything else from the appellant and that the allegation of the appellant being a mastermind is not backed by evidence of extensive dealing with narcotics.
post_offence_conduct: The appellant has been in custody for over 7 years and 4 months, and the trial has progressed slowly with 30 witnesses examined and 34 more to be examined.
bail_history: Appellant enlarged on bail subject to such conditions as the trial court may impose
trial_duration: Offence: 28.09.2015; Trial judgment: 08.09.2022; High Court decision: 08.09.2022; Supreme Court decision: 28.03.2023
legal_representation: Ms. Tanya Agarwal, Mrs. Shubhangi Tuli, Advs. for the Appellant; Vikramjit Banerjee, A.S.G., Shreekant Neelappa Terdal, Ms. Nachiketa Joshi, Digvijay Dam, Sachin Sharma, Rajan Kr. Chourasia, Ms. Shruti Agarwal, Ms. Janhvi Prakash, Kartik Dey, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: Chargesheet filed on 29.02.2016; charges framed on 05.07.2016; supplemental chargesheets filed on 01.08.2016 and 08.11.2017
appeal_history: Trial court: Rejected bail application; High Court: Rejected bail application; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution relied on the statement of co-accused Nitesh Ekka and the confessional statement of the appellant, as well as bank statements of Virender Singh @ Beerey, alleging that the appellant was a mastermind involved in narcotics dealing. However, the prosecution has not recovered anything else from the appellant and lacks evidence of extensive dealing with narcotics.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the appellant has been in custody for over 7 years and 4 months, with the trial progressing at a snail's pace. The appellant is not guilty of the offence and is not likely to commit any offence while on bail, and two co-accused have already been granted bail.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that the grant of bail under Section 37 of the NDPS Act must be considered in the context of the right to speedy trial under Article 21 of the Constitution, balancing the accused's liberty against public interest and ensuring expeditious trial.
precedent_relied_upon: Kartar Singh v. State of Punjab (1994) 3 SCC 569; Supreme Court Legal Aid Committee v. Union of India (1994) 6 SCC 731; Shaheen Welfare Association v. Union of India (1996) 2 SCC 616; Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation (2022) 10 SCC 51; Union of India v. K. A. Najeeb (2021) 3 SCC 713; Vijay Madanlal Chaudhary v. Union of India (2022) 10 SCC 51
judicial_mitigating_factors: The appellant has been in custody for over 7 years and 4 months, and the trial has progressed slowly with only 30 of 64 witnesses examined. The appellant is not likely to commit any offence while on bail.
other_sentence_order: The appellant is directed to be enlarged on bail, subject to such conditions as the trial court may impose.
